column1: # [MIGRATED REPORT PROVENANCE - flagged 2026-09-09] Commit d5cb15b renumbered
#   every ab(...)@2 id in this file to @3 and, in five of the seven refute
#   reports, deleted the time=-opponent rows. This run was performed by the @2
#   binary. Read @3 here as @2, and check the row count against
#   git show d5cb15b^:<this path> before quoting a rate. See Docs/corrections.md.
# rank.exe refute -- one row per (target, colour)
# mined: 1 = the miner found a win, 0 = conceded
# verify: W/L/D for the BOOK's side, replayed through openerBook by the wearer
# blocked_shared: every position on the losing line was owned by an already-won
#   line, so no move could be changed without breaking one. That is the merge
#   conflict a single position-keyed book cannot express.
# audit: 1 = the WRITTEN book won this line replayed on its own. Distinct from
#   `mined`, which only says the line was found while our side was still
# oob_first: the first of OUR moves the book did not serve, so the fallback brain
#   had to choose (-1 = the book covered the whole line). A line with oob_first
#   >= 0 was carried by the brain, not by the book, whatever its result says.
# oob_key: the position hash at oob_first, in the same 16-digit form the
#   book file uses (0 = the book covered the whole line). Match it against
#   the keys the stage-3 collision warning prints, to see whether a line left
#   the book at a position a later winner overwrote, instead of inferring it
# ovr_ply / ovr_key: the first of OUR plies where the written book served a
#   move different from the one the mine recorded at that same position, and
#   the position hash there (-1 / 0 = never). A nonzero ovr_key is a measured
#   overwrite of this line by a later winner, not an inference from oob_first.
#   Blank under --verify-only, which has no mined path to compare against.
# rejected: stage-2 wins refused because committing the line would have
#   overwritten a position an already-won line depends on.
# v_plies: half-moves in the openerBook verification game. A line that matches
#   `plies` played the same length game the miner recorded.
